Some good advice in here and I'll add a few things I haven't seen recommended.

Buy store-brand stuff if available where you get groceries.

Also most items will periodically go on sale/buy-one-get-one with a member's card or the equivalent, those cards are usually free to sign up for and you don't even have to give them any real information from what I can tell, and I've always gotten a card/number to use on the spot. Most stores near me will allow you to just key in a phone number of a card holder to get the discounts, so I don't even carry one and just use a family member's old phone number from 10 years ago that works everywhere.

The trick to taking advantage of the periodic sales though is to stock up on the items you buy when you see them for sale, even if you don't need them yet. Tea, coffee, cereal, whatever. Same goes for meats, freeze whatever you can get on sale. Building up a reserve just helps you to hold off buying things at full price because you suddenly run out. Then if you can make it by the grocery store close to once per week, only buy stuff on sale, and buy a couple of them. Really makes an impact after a while to plan in that way, and helps you to be prepared for any sudden food shortages. I never have to deal with the grocery store panic mobs of mouthbreathers when a hurricane comes around, and I spend less than they do in the process.

Farmer's markets during the summer can be hit or miss but usually a good way to get high quality produce for a good price. Sometimes prices are just garbage though and I don't know why it's so variable, but worth checking out if you have any near you.

Making your own bread can be rewarding and very cost saving if you buy bulk ingredients and otherwise eat a lot of bread, but it is pretty time consuming. You may really enjoy the art of it so I recommend at least trying it a few times. Good skills to have and it's not difficult to make some really good bread.

Last piece of advice would just be to consider shopping in the "shitty" grocery store chain for certain items if your store selection includes that.
